summary: Ukraine is experiencing widespread domestic protests and significant leadership changes, including the dismissal of Prime Minister Sviridenko and the appointment of Klimenko as NCSC Secretary. Large-scale Russian aerial attacks involving ballistic missiles and numerous UAVs have targeted multiple regions, including Odesa and Kharkiv. The conflict is characterized by high-intensity strikes on civilian infrastructure and significant internal political shifts within the Ukrainian government.
key_points: Mass protests are occurring across Ukraine, including Kyiv, Lviv, and Odesa, demanding the resignation of Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi and the return of Fedorov (Source: @DeepStateUA/23660).
President Zelensky has dismissed Prime Minister Yulia Sviridenko and proposed appointing Ihor Klimenko as Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31714).
Russian forces launched a massive aerial attack involving 90 UAVs and ballistic missiles, resulting in 19 hits on various locations (Source: @kpszsu/68985).
A Russian strike on a residential building in Odesa resulted in two deaths and five injuries, including three children (Source: @UkraineNow/82714).
In Kharkiv, a missile strike on the Shevchenkivskyi district killed one 40-year-old man and injured nine others, including two children (Source: @UkraineNow/82734).
Ukrainian UAVs attacked a large Wildberries warehouse in Elektrostal, Moscow region, causing 24 injuries (Source: @eRadarrua/101491).
The EU has imposed new sanctions against Russian entities involved in the production of Shahed and Geran drones (Source: @UkraineNow/82728).
A drone strike in Kherson's Dniprovskyi district injured five people, including several elderly women (Source: @UkraineNow/82716).

sections.executive_summary: Ukraine is facing significant internal instability marked by widespread protests in major cities like Kyiv and Odesa demanding military leadership changes. Simultaneously, Russia has escalated aerial bombardments, utilizing ballistic missiles and large numbers of UAVs against civilian infrastructure and logistics hubs. These developments indicate a dual-front crisis of domestic political pressure and high-intensity kinetic warfare.

points: Widespread protests have emerged in Kyiv, Lviv, Ternopil, Odesa, Vinnytsia, Sumy, and Dnipro, with demonstrators demanding the resignation of Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi and the return of Fedorov (Source: @DeepStateUA/23660).
President Zelensky has dismissed Prime Minister Yulia Sviridenko and appointed Ihor Klimenko as the new Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31714).
The EU has implemented new sanctions targeting five organizations and one individual specifically for their involvement in producing Shahed and Geran drones (Source: @UkraineNow/82728).
In Kharkiv, a missile strike on the Shevchenkivskyi district caused one fatality and nine injuries, including two children (Source: @UkraineNow/82734).
A drone strike in Kherson's Dniprovskyi district injured five people, including a 70-year-old woman (Source: @UkraineNow/82716).
In Odesa, a night missile strike on a residential building killed two people and injured five, including three children (Source: @UkraineNow/82714).
Ukrainian UAVs attacked the second-largest Wildberries warehouse in Elektrostal, Moscow region, resulting in 24 injuries (Source: @eRadarrua/101491).
A fire occurred at a fuel depot in Noginsk, requiring emergency services to respond (Source: @tass_agency/385804).
The Russian government is implementing a new policy starting September 1, 2025, allowing citizens to reclaim life insurance premiums (Source: @tass_agency/385816).
The Hungarian government has launched an investigation into former Foreign Minister Peter Szijjártó regarding alleged contacts with Russia (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31708).
A Russian attack on a Naftogaz gas production facility in the Kharkiv region was reported (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31714).
In Izium, a КАБ (guided bomb) attack injured two children and one 40-year-old man (Source: @UkraineNow/82723).
UAVs were reported over Sumy from the north and Chernihiv from the east (Source: @kpszsu/68963).
A reactive UAV was reported flying from the Sumy region toward Chernihiv via Krolevets (Source: @eRadarrua/101487).
Kherson is expanding mandatory evacuation measures due to the expanding Russian shelling zone (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31716).
Missiles were reported in the Black Sea towards Odesa (Source: @kpszsu/68969).
UAVs were detected in the direction of Odesa from the Black Sea (Source: @kpszsu/68963).
Russia launched a massive strike involving 90 UAVs (including Shahed, Gerbera, and Italmas) and ballistic missiles from Crimea and Russian regions (Source: @kpszsu/68985).
Ukrainian air defense intercepted and destroyed one Kh-59/69 guided air missile and 69 enemy UAVs (Source: @kpszsu/68985).
A threat of Iskander-M ballistic missile launches was reported from Taganrog, Rostov region (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69125).
Russian forces continue strikes against Ukrainian ports used for military logistics (Source: @tass_agency/385801).

sections.threat_assessment: The operational environment is highly volatile due to the convergence of large-scale Russian aerial strikes and significant internal Ukrainian political unrest. The targeting of civilian infrastructure in Odesa and Kharkiv indicates a continued Russian focus on demoralization. The demand for military leadership changes in major cities poses a potential risk to command stability and domestic cohesion.
sections.regional_response: The EU has responded to the escalation by sanctioning drone production entities. Domestically, the Ukrainian government is undergoing rapid leadership shifts, including the appointment of Ihor Klimenko to the NCSC to manage national security amidst the crisis.
sections.intelligence_notes: The arrest of former 155th brigade commander Stanislav Luchanov for criminal activities and the dismissal of the Prime Minister suggest internal friction within the Ukrainian administration. Additionally, the increase in xenophobic crimes against Ukrainians in Poland indicates growing regional tensions in Europe.
